name: Mirrorjaw Market
description: The most notorious recurring ghost market in GLMZ, Mirrorjaw materializes in a different decommissioned infrastructure node every 11-to-19 days — abandoned water treatment bays, sealed transit switching stations, the gutted lower floors of foreclosed corporate towers. Vendors sell unregistered geneware mods, Underworld BCI plugins, pre-Corponation archival data, and contraband food grown in unlicensed vertical plots. Entry is by invitation chain only: each attendee may vouch for one new person per cycle, making the social network self-policing. The market takes its name from the original 2207 location — a mirrored-tile maintenance corridor beneath the old Jawline elevated rail.
cultural_impact: Mirrorjaw has become a cultural institution as much as a market — musicians perform, artists sell physical works, and community disputes get arbitrated by the market's rotating steward council. It represents one of the few the Gray Zone spaces where Tier 1 and Tier 2 residents interact as equals rather than client and service provider.
key_figures: Odalys Ferreira-Sung (founding steward, whereabouts currently unknown)
Brekke (synthetic vendor known for pre-Corponation data recovery, no last name registered)
Tomasz Achebe-Lindqvist (Tier 2 fixer who runs the invitation chain logistics)
locations: Jawline Rail Understructure, the Gray Zone Sector 7 (original, now sealed)
Rotating — most recently reported at Filtration Bay 9, Northwest Water Reclamation District
Sublevel 3, Foreclosed Dakarai-Moss Tower, Tier 2 border
story_hooks: Someone is selling authenticated pre-Corponation legal documents at Mirrorjaw that could void a major land claim — three corponations want them destroyed and one mysterious buyer wants them intact.
The invitation chain has been compromised; a corporate informant has been attending for six cycles, and the steward council needs someone outside their network to identify who.
A first-time attendee witnesses a transaction they were never meant to see — a Tier 4 corporate executive buying something that has no legal name.
